# Replace with a precise, decision-oriented title

> Evidence status: State what is confirmed, reproduced, proposed, illustrative, or
> awaiting author confirmation.

## Executive summary

State the decision, primary risk, recommended control strategy, and material
residual risk.

## Scope and non-goals

Define systems, identities, data classes, environments, and excluded concerns.

## Assumptions and constraints

List the conditions on which the design depends.

## Assets, actors, and trust boundaries

Include a Mermaid data-flow or trust-boundary diagram when it clarifies the design.

## Threat model and abuse cases

Connect each material abuse case to controls and tests.

## Architecture decision record

Document the selected option, alternatives, decision drivers, and consequences.

## Control design

Map preventive, detective, and responsive controls to threats. Identify control
owners and dependencies.

## Failure modes

Describe missing context, dependency failure, bypass identities, rollback failure,
partial deployment, and unsafe operator behavior.

## Implementation

Label every code block `tested`, `partially tested`, `illustrative`, or `pseudocode`.

## Deployment and rollback

Describe prerequisites, phased rollout, go/no-go evidence, rollback triggers, and
data-migration implications.

## Validation evidence

Link runnable tests. Include expected results, negative cases, tool versions, and
validation gaps.

## Observability and operations

Define logs, metrics, alerts, runbooks, review cadence, and incident-response hooks.

## Residual risk, cost, and usability

Be explicit about what remains possible and which trade-offs were accepted.

## Limitations

Record evidence gaps and conditions in which the guidance does not apply.
